newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin ends fiscal 1996 with $581 mln balance.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin ends fiscal 1996 with $581 mln balance.

text.p: Wisconsin closed its books on fiscal 1996 with a general fund balance of $581 million, the state's budget director said Wednesday.
Richard Chandler said the balance represents about seven percent of the $8.16 million the state spent during the fiscal year that ended June 30.
He added the balance was $15 million higher than the state's previous estimate of $566.3 million.

However, Chandler pointed out that Wisconsin will not end the current fiscal year with an equally high balance due to the state's statutory obligation to fund two-thirds of the cost of primary and secondary schools.
"We'll be drawing (the balance) down to reach the two-thirds school funding level," he said.
He said the ending general fund balance for fiscal year 1997 is expected to be $115 million.

Chandler disputed a recent Wisconsin Legislative Fiscal Bureau report that said spending pressures for schools and prisons and limited increases in revenues could cause a nearly $390 million deficit in the state's upcoming fiscal 1998-99 biennial budget.
He said that the state's economy remains strong and that the administration of Gov. Tommy Thompson believes the budget can be balanced without tax increases.
Thompson's proposed budget is scheduled to be introduced in the legislature sometime in late January or early February, Chandler said.
